current_bottleneck: The hard broad-frame 510a failures still look signal-limited rather than encoder-shape-limited. last_result_summary: 600a audited whether local-geometry IV-history features are a justified next architecture move. Focused tests passed. On 441 broad-frame windows with 48 510a samples, pure LGA features lost to IV summaries on bad-window <50% coverage (R2 lift -0.9025, AUC lift -0.1235), window coverage (R2 lift -1.0685), persistent-undercoverage count (R2 lift -1.1746), and level absolute error (R2 lift -3.7238). Adding LGA to summaries also hurt these core targets, though it weakly improved median-bias fraction by R2 +0.3725 while remaining negative in absolute R2.
next_step_recommendation: Do not escalate local-geometry attention into the generator now. The next principled step is research ideation or a post-experiment boundary decision: either separate base learned-law metrics from a disclosed risk-policy overlay for risk-manager deployment, or identify genuinely new signal/objective framing before another architecture change.
